## 🌎 Geopolitics

### Iran's Revolutionary Guard claims two oil tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz, escalating sea crisis

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on November 1 that two tankers, including a very large crude carrier (VLCC), struck mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz near the route 25 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, Oman. One vessel reportedly burst into flames; Iran claimed the ships had disabled tracking systems and navigated through prohibited waters. The incidents follow October 30 reports of an attack by small boats attaching explosives to a tanker hull, and come as tensions over a potential U.S. strike on Iran loom after the U.S. midterm elections.

**Why it matters.** The Strait of Hormuz handles roughly one-third of global maritime oil trade—any disruption feeds directly into energy prices, inflation, and market volatility that hits India's import-dependent oil sector and your consulting clients' cost structures. If this escalates to wider U.S.-Iran strikes (a live possibility once election dust settles), shipping insurance premiums spike, supply chains lock up, and the rupee typically weakens against the dollar. For quant/prop strategies, the next 48 hours will define November's oil curve and energy equity performance. India has been monitoring the strait closely given its own energy security dependence and regional positioning.

**Action.** Track oil futures (WTI, Brent) and the UKMTO incident log for the next reports on these two vessels' status. Read the recent CNBC coverage on U.S. military posturing toward Iran, and set alerts on shipping indices like the Baltic Dry Index and tanker rate premiums. If confirmed strikes happen, expect a fast repricing in energy and emerging-market FX.

*Sources: [jpost.com](https://www.jpost.com/middle-east/iran-news/article-913514) · [aninews.in](https://aninews.in/news/world/middle-east/2-tankers-explode-after-allegedly-hitting-naval-mines-in-strait-of-hormuz-iran-claims20261102050020/) · [trend.az](https://www.trend.az/world/4241715.html)*

### India approves $22 billion defense modernization push focused on AI, drones, and counter-China capability

New Delhi's government approved approximately $22 billion (2.12 trillion rupees) in military spending on October 29 to modernize defense equipment and close capability gaps with China, particularly in next-generation platforms, cyber, space assets, and AI-enabled systems. The package includes procurement of long-range drones, advanced surveillance infrastructure, and anti-drone technology; 82 percent of the equipment is planned to come from domestic suppliers, while foreign companies will provide key technology. This represents a 10-year high in annual defense approval value and is the largest single-year modernization push in India's recent budget cycle.

**Why it matters.** This is direct India exposure—a $22 billion domestic procurement cycle will ripple through Indian defense contractors, component suppliers, and tech firms over the next three to five years. The emphasis on AI-enabled systems and drone autonomy opens consulting opportunities in defense tech advisory and supply-chain risk modeling. Geopolitically, it signals New Delhi's pivot toward operational deterrence against China rather than diplomatic hedging, which reshapes regional balance-of-power assumptions and affects FDI calculus for any India-focused quant book. The domestic-sourcing mandate also reflects the Modi administration's "Atmanirbhar" push—nationalist economic policy that could tighten foreign vendor access and reshape procurement timelines.

**Action.** Research the list of approved contracts once released (watch Ministry of Defence tenders and the Defense Acquisition Council circulars). Track Bharat Electronics, HAL, L&T, and other Indian defense contractors for Q3 announcements. Set up a conversation with India-focused investment advisors to understand how this shifts defense-sector valuations and defense supply-chain concentration risk. Note the technology transfer angles with foreign OEMs—those agreements will define India's indigenous capability curve over the next decade.

*Sources: [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/29/india-china-us-israel-military-spending.html) · [newsbytesapp.com](https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/india/india-invests-rs212000cr-to-modernize-military-amid-china-tensions/tldr) · [azernews.az](https://www.azernews.az/analysis/253870.html)*

## 🧠 Artificial Intelligence

### Anthropic Files S-1 for Public Listing; Revenue $16.3B in H1 2026

Anthropic filed Form S-1 with the SEC on October 26, 2026, seeking a Nasdaq listing under ticker "ANT." The filing discloses $16.3 billion in revenue for the first half of 2026, up 13.6x from $1.2 billion in the same period of 2025. Net losses totaled $80.7 billion for the six-month period (including $72.4 billion in fair-value changes). The company counts 11,900+ customers with $100,000 or more annualized revenue as of September 30, 2026. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are lead underwriters on a 22-firm syndicate; IPO timing is not confirmed, but press reports suggest mid-to-late November.

**Why it matters.** This signals the first major AI lab headed to public markets with both extreme scale (reported pre-IPO valuation ~$2 trillion, pending SEC effectiveness) and demonstrated revenue traction. For AI engineers, the filing's disclosures—revenue growth rate, customer concentration, infrastructure burn—become public knowledge, reshaping how the frontier lab financing game is understood. The cash infusion will directly compete with OpenAI and Google for compute allocation and researcher retention in a capital-constrained chip market.

**Action.** Read the S-1 filing on EDGAR (once SEC effectiveness is declared) to benchmark customer concentration, gross margins, and infrastructure capex guidance. The revenue and loss figures will set the template for how other labs must eventually disclose—watch for OpenAI and Google to adopt similar public-market disclosure timelines.

*Sources: [[Anthropic Files S-1 for IPO, Plans to List on Nasdaq as 'ANT'](https://coinmarketcap.com/academy/article/anthropic-files-s1-ipo-nasdaq-ant)]([Anthropic Files S-1 for IPO, Plans to List on Nasdaq as 'ANT'](https://coinmarketcap.com/academy/article/anthropic-files-s1-ipo-nasdaq-ant)) · [[Anthropic files for IPO, plans Nasdaq listing under ANT](https://www.mobihealthnews.com/news/anthropic-files-ipo-plans-nasdaq-listing-under-ant)]([Anthropic files for IPO, plans Nasdaq listing under ANT](https://www.mobihealthnews.com/news/anthropic-files-ipo-plans-nasdaq-listing-under-ant)) · [[Anthropic IPO Filing: $80.7B Loss, $16.3B Revenue [2026]](https://tech-insider.org/anthropic-ipo-s-1-filing-ant-nasdaq-16-3b-revenue-2026/)]([Anthropic IPO Filing: $80.7B Loss, $16.3B Revenue [2026]](https://tech-insider.org/anthropic-ipo-s-1-filing-ant-nasdaq-16-3b-revenue-2026/))*

### AMD MI355X Serves Kimi K3 at 2.3x Lower Cost Than Nvidia B200

SemiAnalysis's InferenceX benchmark, published October 31, shows AMD's MI355X achieving inference throughput at $0.077 per million tokens on Kimi K3 (a 1.5TB+ parameter model) versus $0.179 on Nvidia's B200—a 2.3x cost advantage. Both GPUs offer 288GB of VRAM, allowing Kimi K3's weights to fit on a single 8-GPU node, while B200 requires cross-node sharding with associated latency penalties. The gap widens under certain configurations and narrows under others depending on assumed GPU rental rates and batch sizes.

**Why it matters.** This is the first hard evidence that AMD can achieve competitive inference economics on frontier models at scale. For engineers deploying large agents or multi-turn agentic workloads, the per-token math now favors AMD—but only if you can access MI355X capacity and tolerate day-one software immaturity on inference frameworks. The memory-per-GPU economics flip the script: constrained token budgets now mean AMD's extra memory is a real moat, not a curiosity. Expect cloud providers to rapidly expand MI355X offerings and software vendors to chase optimization on CDNA 4.

**Action.** If you own inference infrastructure decisions: run InferenceX on your specific model and batch profile (results vary by use case). Benchmark MI355X against B200 in your target cloud provider's actual rental rates, not SemiAnalysis's assumptions. If you're a framework maintainer: prioritize Kimi K3 / frontier model kernels on CDNA 4 to claim the software optimization moat.

*Sources: [[Nvidia B200 Costs Up to 2.3x AMD MI355X per Kimi K3 Token - FourWeekMBA](https://fourweekmba.com/ai-nvidia-b200-costs-up-to-2-3x-amd-mi355x-per-kimi-k3-token/)]([Nvidia B200 Costs Up to 2.3x AMD MI355X per Kimi K3 Token - FourWeekMBA](https://fourweekmba.com/ai-nvidia-b200-costs-up-to-2-3x-amd-mi355x-per-kimi-k3-token/)) · [[SemiAnalysis InferenceX: Kimi K3 on B200 vs MI355X](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/compare-per-dollar/kimi-k3-gb200-vs-mi355x)]([SemiAnalysis InferenceX: Kimi K3 on B200 vs MI355X](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/compare-per-dollar/kimi-k3-gb200-vs-mi355x)) · [[AMD MI355X beats Nvidia B300 on cost per GPU running Kimi K3](https://glonce.com/amd-mi355x-beats-nvidia-b300-on-cost-per/)]([AMD MI355X beats Nvidia B300 on cost per GPU running Kimi K3](https://glonce.com/amd-mi355x-beats-nvidia-b300-on-cost-per/))*

## 🇮🇳 India

### Unacademy Founders Launch ₹700 Crore Longshot Capital Fund for Indian AI and Deeptech

Gaurav Munjal and Roman Saini, co-founders of Unacademy, have launched Longshot Capital, a Category II Alternative Investment Fund targeting ₹700 crore in capital for early-stage AI and deeptech startups. The fund has ₹250–300 crore in commitments so far, with Saini running it full-time while Munjal maintains his role at Unacademy as part-time general partner. First close is targeted for January 2027, with initial deployment cheques between $500,000 and $1.5 million per company.

**Why it matters.** This signals substantial new capital flowing directly into India's deeptech infrastructure at a critical moment. For an AI engineer building in India, it means venture capital is actively hunting founders in language models, agent infrastructure, manufacturing AI, and robotics—beyond the saturated consumer apps space. The fund's track record includes 200+ angel investments deploying over ₹25 crore, so it will back engineers credible enough to raise institutional money. It also validates that India's top ed-tech founder sees the deeptech opportunity as his next wealth-creation frontier, not a passive LP play.

**Action.** Track Longshot Capital's first close announcements (likely January 2027 via Crunchbase, Inc42). For those building in deeptech, audit your deck for the fund's thesis areas: AI infrastructure, manufacturing, space, defence, and robotics. Check Munjal and Saini's personal angel portfolios on CB Insights to understand their conviction pattern.

*Sources: [[Inc42: Unacademy Cofounders Plan ₹700 Cr AI, Deeptech Fund](https://inc42.com/buzz/unacademy-cofounders-plan-₹700-cr-ai-deeptech-fund/)]([Inc42: Unacademy Cofounders Plan ₹700 Cr AI, Deeptech Fund](https://inc42.com/buzz/unacademy-cofounders-plan-₹700-cr-ai-deeptech-fund/)) · [[The Outpost: Unacademy Founders Launch ₹700 Cr AI Fund](https://theoutpost.ai/news-story/unacademy-founders-launch-700-cr-ai-and-deeptech-fund-longshot-capital-with-300-cr-committed-32634/)]([The Outpost: Unacademy Founders Launch ₹700 Cr AI Fund](https://theoutpost.ai/news-story/unacademy-founders-launch-700-cr-ai-and-deeptech-fund-longshot-capital-with-300-cr-committed-32634/)) · [[Product Growth: Unacademy Cofounders Plan ₹700 Cr AI Deeptech Fund](https://productgrowth.in/news/2026-10-27/unacademy-cofounders-plan-700-cr-ai-deeptech-fund/)]([Product Growth: Unacademy Cofounders Plan ₹700 Cr AI Deeptech Fund](https://productgrowth.in/news/2026-10-27/unacademy-cofounders-plan-700-cr-ai-deeptech-fund/))*

### Matiks Raises $10 Million from General Catalyst to Scale AI-Powered Puzzle Gaming Globally

Bengaluru-based social gaming startup Matiks secured $10 million in pre-Series A funding led by US venture firm General Catalyst, with participation from Ronnie Screwvala and existing backers Info Edge Ventures, Tanglin Venture Partners, and Untitled Ventures. Daily active users surged from 22,000 in early 2026 to over 300,000 by September. The capital will fuel expansion into Japan and South Korea, and scale Jelo, an experimental AI tool for rapid game prototyping that reduces iteration cycles.

**Why it matters.** This demonstrates that product-led user growth still commands premium venture valuations, even in a crowded gaming market. For engineers in fintech or AI consulting eyeing product-market fit, Matiks is a case study: strong unit economics (300K DAU), fast iteration velocity (General Catalyst partner Rahul Humayan cited this specifically), and clear expansion playbook. It also shows US-tier VCs are actively deploying capital into Indian consumer gaming again, not just enterprise AI, which changes the competitive landscape for hiring talent and capital allocation.

**Action.** Pull Matiks' publicly disclosed deck or analyst notes on their Series A metrics (user retention, LTV:CAC, churn rates) once the round closes. Watch for their Japan/South Korea launch announcements to understand how Indian gaming studios localize for Asian markets. If you're building AI tools for creators or developers, study their Jelo tool's positioning—it's a B2B AI wedge into consumer game studios.

*Sources: [[TechCrunch: Matiks Raises $10M for Puzzle Gaming Platform](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/26/matiks-raises-10m-to-expand-its-math-and-puzzle-gaming-platform/)]([TechCrunch: Matiks Raises $10M for Puzzle Gaming Platform](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/26/matiks-raises-10m-to-expand-its-math-and-puzzle-gaming-platform/)) · [[Inc42: Matiks Bags $10 Mn To Take Its Puzzle Gaming Platform Global](https://inc42.com/buzz/matiks-bags-10-mn-to-take-puzzle-gaming-platform-global/)]([Inc42: Matiks Bags $10 Mn To Take Its Puzzle Gaming Platform Global](https://inc42.com/buzz/matiks-bags-10-mn-to-take-puzzle-gaming-platform-global/)) · [[YourStory: Matiks Raises $10M in Pre-Series A Round](https://yourstory.com/2026/10/matiks-raises-10-million-pre-series-a-round-general-catalyst)]([YourStory: Matiks Raises $10M in Pre-Series A Round](https://yourstory.com/2026/10/matiks-raises-10-million-pre-series-a-round-general-catalyst))*

## 🇮🇳 Indian Stocks

### TRENT (NSE): +5.44% on 25% Q2 profit growth to ₹468 crore

Trent shot up 5.44% to ₹3,017.30 on October 30 after releasing Q2 results showing consolidated net profit swelling 25% year-on-year to ₹468 crore. Revenue climbed 22% to ₹5,873 crore. The apparel and retail group's operating EBITDA margin expanded 37%, pointing to operating leverage as the fast-fashion segment continues to outpace Sensex sluggishness.

**Why it matters.** Trent's acceleration amid a 12% decline in the Nifty 50 this calendar year signals resilience in discretionary consumption and organized retail. The stock's 25% PAT growth — the fastest in the Nifty universe — suggests that urban demand remains intact despite rupee weakness and FPI outflows hammering IT and finance. Standalone profit rose only 9%, so growth is being driven by consolidated subsidiaries, underscoring the value of the group's diversification into e-commerce and supply chain. For engineers in metros like Hyderabad watching domestic demand, this validates that consumer spending has bifurcated: mass-market pressure but premium/fashion performing.

**Action.** Review the filed earnings release on the NSE website (announcements section under TRENT) for the breakdown of subsidiary contributions and same-store sales growth by format. Watch the ₹3,100 level for resistance; the intraday high on October 30 was ₹3,060. The next catalyst is likely Q3 pre-results broker estimates in late December, and the company's February full-year guidance call.

*Sources: [[Trent Q2 net profit rises 23% to ₹464 crore on strong apparel sales](https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/trent-q2-net-profit-rises-23-to-464-crore-on-strong-apparel-sales-126102901089_1.html)]([Trent Q2 net profit rises 23% to ₹464 crore on strong apparel sales](https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/trent-q2-net-profit-rises-23-to-464-crore-on-strong-apparel-sales-126102901089_1.html)) · [[Trent Q2 results: PAT rises 25% to Rs 468 crore YoY; revenue up 22%](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/trent-q2-results-pat-rises-25-to-rs-468-crore-yoy-revenue-up-22-564597-2026-10-29)]([Trent Q2 results: PAT rises 25% to Rs 468 crore YoY; revenue up 22%](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/trent-q2-results-pat-rises-25-to-rs-468-crore-yoy-revenue-up-22-564597-2026-10-29)) · [[Trent Share Price in Focus; Q2 Revenue Rises 22%, Consolidated Profit Jumps 25%](https://www.angelone.in/news/stocks/trent-share-price-in-focus-q2-revenue-rises-22-consolidated-profit-jumps-25%)]([Trent Share Price in Focus; Q2 Revenue Rises 22%, Consolidated Profit Jumps 25%](https://www.angelone.in/news/stocks/trent-share-price-in-focus-q2-revenue-rises-22-consolidated-profit-jumps-25%))*

### INDIGO (NSE): +4.33% as Q2 loss narrows to ₹1,879 crore from ₹2,582 crore

IndiGo climbed 4.33% on October 30 after narrowing its Q2 net loss to ₹1,879 crore from ₹2,582 crore a year prior, even as revenue expanded 26% to ₹243 billion. Operating EBITDA nearly tripled to ₹1,908 crore from ₹579 crore, signalling the low-cost carrier is moving past the worst of fuel and forex headwinds that hammered aviation in 2025.

**Why it matters.** The 27% year-on-year improvement in loss magnitude — with EBITDA jumping despite 4.7% lower passenger volumes — vindicates the strategy of aggressive capacity deployment and fuel hedging that IndiGo has been executing. A ₹1,333 crore forex loss (compared to ₹2,892 crore last year) shows the rupee stabilized relative to the prior-year period, reducing one of aviation's key volatility drags. The margin recovery matters to broader Indian equities because IndiGo is a proxy for both travel demand (domestic consumption) and FX risk; a narrowing loss signals both are stabilizing after quarter of acute distress in energy and currency markets.

**Action.** Cross-reference the full filing on the NSE's corporate actions database and the earnings call transcript (Investing.com hosts it) for commentary on October–November capacity addition, fuel price hedges, and rupee forwarding decisions. IndiGo's cash balance stood at ₹52,685 crore (₹39,929 crore unencumbered) as of September 30, so liquidity is not a concern. Watch ₹145–150 for the next resistance zone; the October 30 close was near the lower end of that range. Macro flows — FPI inflows and crude prices — will drive the stock more than fundamentals until Q3 booking trends surface in late November.

## 🏗 Tech & Startups

### DoorDash bids $17 billion for Instacart, consolidating two giants to counter Walmart and Amazon

DoorDash announced on October 29 it will acquire Instacart for $17 billion, or $65 per share—a 26 percent premium to Instacart's pre-deal close on October 22. The all-cash-heavy deal (at least 75 percent paid in cash, with stock capped at 25 percent consideration) is expected to close in late 2027 or early 2028, pending shareholder approval and regulatory clearance. JPMorgan Chase provided a $13 billion bridge financing commitment.

**Why it matters.** This is the most significant consolidation in U.S. delivery-as-a-service in years, and it signals a fundamental market dynamic: both companies face margin pressure from bigger rivals with deeper pockets. Instacart's market share fell from 26 percent five years ago to 18 percent today, and DoorDash saw the opportunity to fold it into a combined entity that can compete with Amazon Fresh and Walmart+, where neither company alone could. The deal also sends a signal to founders that scale, not profitability, can still justify large valuations when strategic synergies align.

**Action.** Watch for antitrust filings and scrutiny from the Federal Trade Commission—a combined DoorDash-Instacart will face significant regulatory pushback. Founders in logistics, grocery tech, and fintech should track how the FTC responds. If approved, this accelerates consolidation across fragmented delivery markets globally.

### Kalshi hits $40 billion valuation in $1 billion raise as prediction markets race toward IPO

Prediction market platform Kalshi closed a $1 billion Series G on October 29 at a $40 billion post-money valuation, nearly doubling from $22 billion five months prior. Sequoia Capital and Wellington Management co-led the round. The company now claims 30 million accounts and more than 75 percent of prediction market trading volume globally, with annualized revenue reported at $4 billion.

**Why it matters.** Kalshi's rapid ascent—from $2 billion (June 2025) to $40 billion (October 2026)—illustrates how prediction markets have shifted from niche gambling to institutional infrastructure. The company is expanding beyond election and sports betting into stock-linked perpetual futures, indices, and computing cost markets, positioning itself as an exchange alternative. This playbook (trading nostalgia + financial products) mirrors how crypto exchanges added derivatives. Founders in fintech and trading infrastructure should note that regulatory uncertainty (Utah just charged Kalshi execs with illegal gambling promotion) hasn't stopped venture or investor appetite.

**Action.** Watch for Kalshi's IPO filing in 2027 and track whether the SEC or CFTC clarifies regulatory status for prediction markets before a public listing. Competitors Polymarket and others are following the same path. If Kalshi successfully IPOs despite legal challenges, it signals a green light for founders building real-money trading platforms.

## 🩹 Health & Science

### Common Cancer Mutations Reshape DNA Topology Through CTCF Binding

Researchers published in Nature (October 28, 2026) discovered how mutations in the BAF chromatin complex—present in roughly 20% of human cancers across nearly all tumor types—alter DNA folding by creating new binding sites for CTCF. First author Darko Barisic and colleagues ran genomic analysis showing that BAF loss opens thousands of DNA sites, allowing CTCF to bind at novel locations and reshape 3D chromatin architecture. In animal models, deleting CTCF reversed the growth-promoting effects of BAF mutations.

**Why it matters.** This mechanism explains how a single class of mutations drives cancer across diverse tissue types. The work identifies CTCF, PBAB, and ISWI as potential therapeutic targets, offering a concrete path for drug developers. Unlike treating individual cancer types in isolation, a CTCF-targeting approach could address 20% of the entire cancer genome in one mechanism.

**Action.** Clinicians should follow clinical trials targeting CTCF in BAF-mutant cancers starting 2027. Researchers should validate PBAF and ISWI as independent therapeutic levers. The Nature paper (s41586-026-11197-w) provides the full mechanism and therapeutic rationale.

*Sources: [[Nature: SWI/SNF complexes shape 3D chromatin architecture through CTCF and cohesin](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11197-w)]([Nature: SWI/SNF complexes shape 3D chromatin architecture through CTCF and cohesin](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11197-w)) · [[Cornell News: A unifying mechanism for cancer-driving mutations](https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2026/10/unifying-mechanism-cancer-driving-mutations)]([Cornell News: A unifying mechanism for cancer-driving mutations](https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2026/10/unifying-mechanism-cancer-driving-mutations)) · [[Medical Xpress: Study identifies common mechanism behind widespread cancer mutations](https://www.news-medical.net/news/20261028/Study-identifies-common-mechanism-behind-widespread-cancer-mutations.aspx)]([Medical Xpress: Study identifies common mechanism behind widespread cancer mutations](https://www.news-medical.net/news/20261028/Study-identifies-common-mechanism-behind-widespread-cancer-mutations.aspx))*

### Johns Hopkins Solves 15-Year Mystery: Toxin Receptor Claudin-4 Offers Path to Colorectal Cancer Prevention

Johns Hopkins Medicine researchers announced October 31, 2026, findings from a Nature paper (published April 22, 2026) identifying claudin-4 as the host cell receptor that Bacteroides fragilis toxin (BFT) uses to damage the colon. Senior authors Cynthia Sears and Min Dong conducted a genome-wide CRISPR screen in colon epithelial cells showing that removing claudin-4 prevented BFT binding and left E-cadherin intact. The team then engineered a soluble claudin-4 decoy that captured the toxin and protected mouse intestinal lining from damage.

**Why it matters.** The 20-year suspicion that BFT drives chronic inflammation and colorectal cancer now has a molecular basis, opening a preventive strategy. The decoy receptor strategy bypasses the need for drugs; a claudin-4 competitor could be delivered to high-risk populations (those carrying toxigenic Bacteroides strains) to block damage before it starts. This bridges microbiome risk stratification with actionable therapeutics.

**Action.** Identify high-risk populations carrying toxigenic Bacteroides strains via microbiome sequencing. Test the claudin-4 decoy in Phase 1b trials for safety and durability in recurrent colitis and colorectal adenomas. The Nature paper provides structural and functional data needed for clinical formulation.

*Sources: [[Nature: A pro-carcinogenic bacterial toxin binds claudin-4 to cleave E-cadherin](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10375-0)]([Nature: A pro-carcinogenic bacterial toxin binds claudin-4 to cleave E-cadherin](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10375-0)) · [[ScienceDaily: Scientists finally discover how a common gut bacterium can trigger colon cancer](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/10/261031012912.htm)]([ScienceDaily: Scientists finally discover how a common gut bacterium can trigger colon cancer](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/10/261031012912.htm)) · [[SciTechDaily: Researchers Solve 15-Year Mystery Behind Cancer-Causing Gut Toxin](https://scitechdaily.com/researchers-solve-15-year-mystery-behind-cancer-causing-gut-toxin/)]([SciTechDaily: Researchers Solve 15-Year Mystery Behind Cancer-Causing Gut Toxin](https://scitechdaily.com/researchers-solve-15-year-mystery-behind-cancer-causing-gut-toxin/))*
